title: Observing relativistic trajectories of single photons
authors: Sayantan Das, Daniel S. Dahl, Daniel Peace, Marcelo P. Almeida, Abhishek Roy, Markus Rambach, Andrew G. White, Timothy C. Ralph, Jacquiline Romero
abstract: While the standard interpretation of quantum mechanics does not assign definite trajectories to particles, the Bohmian interpretation does. Only recently has an operational method for reconciling Bohmian mechanics with relativity been proposed. Here, we experimentally reconstruct relativistic Bohmian trajectories of a single photon in a Michelson-Sagnac interferometer, where counter-propagating probability amplitudes interfere head-on at the speed of light. As predicted by the relativistic Bohmian theory, we observe subluminal and superluminal features of the Bohmian trajectories of the photon traversing through the fringes. Our work provides experimental access to relativistic Bohmian mechanics and enables exploration of its unusual and counterintuitive properties.
summary: This paper experimentally investigates relativistic Bohmian mechanics by measuring the trajectory of a single photon in a Michelson-Sagnac interferometer. By weakly measuring path information, the authors reconstruct the Bohmian velocity, observing characteristic subluminal and superluminal deviations from the speed of light. This provides novel experimental access to the deterministic, yet counterintuitive, predictions of Bohmian theory in a relativistic context.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of reconciling Bohmian mechanics, which posits definite particle trajectories, with the principles of special relativity, specifically by experimentally reconstructing the relativistic Bohmian trajectory of a single photon.
main_result: The experiment successfully observed subluminal and superluminal features in the reconstructed Bohmian trajectories as the photon passes through interference fringes, confirming predictions of relativistic Bohmian theory.
method: The measurement protocol involves weakly measuring 'which-path' information in a Michelson-Sagnac interferometer using the photon's polarization degree of freedom to reconstruct the relativistic Bohmian velocity $v(x)$.
model_or_system: The physical system is a single photon propagating through a Michelson-Sagnac interferometer. The theoretical framework is relativistic Bohmian mechanics, which predicts the velocity $v(x) = j_x/ho$ based on the probability current and density.
key_observables: The primary observable is the relativistic Bohmian velocity $v(x)$, which is reconstructed from the ratio of average photon counts ($\langle\hat{N}_1 - \hat{N}_2angle / \langle\hat{N}_1 + \hat{N}_2angle$).
important_parameters: The key parameters include the amplitude splitting ratio $\eta$ (or related $\delta$), the relative phase $\phi(x)$, and the measurement beam-splitter position $x$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes natural units ($c = \hbar = 1$), utilizes the optical approximation, and relies on the assumption that all particles passing through a point follow the same deterministic trajectory.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the conceptual setup for head-on interference. Figure 2 shows the velocity-vector-angle $\chi$ vs. MBS position for varying splitting ratios. Figure 3 compares theoretical and experimental trajectories overlaid on probability densities, demonstrating the curvature of the path.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the theoretical necessity of reconciling Bohmian mechanics with relativity. It then details the experimental platform using a Michelson-Sagnac interferometer and weak measurement techniques. Finally, it presents the quantitative results, comparing the measured velocity profile to the theoretical predictions, highlighting the subluminal/superluminal features.
why_interesting: This work provides a direct, experimental test of a non-standard interpretation of quantum mechanics (Bohmian mechanics) in a relativistic setting, which is highly relevant to foundational quantum physics and quantum optics.
